text:
**Refined prompt:** Answer whether this NestJS RealWorld API permits another user to edit an article they don't own — from the code, not from the Swagger annotations — and say what the code does and doesn't let you determine about who did it. · Assumptions: "our API" = the TypeORM implementation on `master` (the `prisma/` folder is explicitly out of scope per CURRENT_FOCUS.md:22).

Yes. It's not a bug you'd have to get lucky to hit — it's the default behaviour of `PUT /api/articles/:slug`.

## The path

`ArticleController.update()` (`src/article/article.controller.ts:60`) takes only `@Param()` and `@Body('article')`. It never receives the caller's identity at all — no `@User('id')`, unlike `create()` on line 52 which does. It passes straight through:

```ts
// article.controller.ts:60-63
async update(@Param() params, @Body('article') articleData: CreateArticleDto) {
  return this.articleService.update(params.slug, articleData);
}
```

And the service (`src/article/article.service.ts:190-195`) loads by slug and saves:

```ts
let toUpdate = await this.articleRepository.findOne({ slug: slug});
let updated = Object.assign(toUpdate, articleData);
```

There is no line anywhere in that chain comparing the caller to `article.author`. The `@ApiResponse({ status: 403, description: 'Forbidden.' })` on `article.controller.ts:58` documents a check that was never written.

**What it does require:** a valid token. `PUT articles/:slug` is in the middleware list (`src/article/article.module.ts:27`), so `AuthMiddleware` runs — but it only resolves the token to *a* user (`src/user/auth.middleware.ts:17-18`) and calls `next()`. Any registered account will do. Same story for `DELETE /articles/:slug` (`article.controller.ts:69`).

## Two things that make it worse than "they changed my text"

- **`Object.assign` persists whatever they sent.** `findOne({slug})` loads the article without relations, so `author` is unset on the loaded entity — a body containing `"author": {"id": <theirs>}` or `"id": <n>` would be merged in and saved. I have not executed this to confirm TypeORM's exact write, but nothing in the code prevents the assignment, and there's no validation pipe on this route (unlike `POST /users` at `user.controller.ts:31`). This is LESSONS.md #112 again.
- **Tokens last 60 days and can't be revoked.** `generateJWT` sets `exp` at +60 days (`src/user/user.service.ts:103-113`) and there is no denylist. Anyone who held a token in the last two months still holds it.

## On finding out who

You likely can't, from the app. I grepped `src/` for `logger|Logger|morgan|audit|winston` — **no matches**. Nothing records request identity.

The one thing you do have: `ArticleEntity.updateTimestamp()` is `@BeforeUpdate()` (`src/article/article.entity.ts:29-32`), so the `updated` column holds the time of the edit. That gives you *when*, which you can cross-reference against a reverse proxy / DB access log if you keep one. It will not give you *who*.

## Adjacent, since you're assessing exposure

`DELETE /api/users/:slug` (`src/user/user.controller.ts:37-40`) is not in any `configure()` block — no token required at all — and `UserService.delete()` deletes by the value in `:slug`, which is matched against email. That one is worse than the article case.

**What I did not read:** the `prisma/` folder, the test files, and any deployment/proxy config outside this repo — so I can't tell you what a WAF or gateway in front of this might be filtering.

---

Ownership checks on `PUT/DELETE /articles/:slug` are already item 2 in CURRENT_FOCUS.md:10, marked "design first." Want me to draft that design — where the check goes (controller vs service), how `403` gets raised, and the loaded-relation problem, since `findOne({slug})` doesn't currently load `author` to compare against?
